reader.requirement: After an indexed WRITE, control goes per IX.1.3.5: invalid key -> the INVALID KEY phrase (USE not run) or, when absent, the USE procedure; success with no exception (00 or 02) -> the NOT INVALID KEY phrase; an unsuccessful non-invalid-key outcome (44, 48) -> the USE procedure and neither phrase.

edition-consulted.switches: ctx.Data.DialectLevel >= 2002 adds the SORT GR17 USE-exit filter to __RunUse; 85 takes the plain try/finally arm (no SORT is active on these WRITE paths, so the USE procedure runs and returns the same way)

reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition|DialectBehavior|DialectLevel|CobolVersion' over IndexedConnector.cs, KeyedConnector.cs, KeyedStore.cs, FileRegistry.cs, FileSupport.cs (only READ, CLOSE WITH LOCK and sharing sites; none in IndexedConnector#Write, #Opened, KeyedConnector#RecordWriteFailed); the same grep over KeyedIoEmitter.cs, SequentialIoEmitter.cs, EcEmitter.cs, DispatchEmitter.cs, UseTierEmitter.cs (DialectLevel only passed to registration, SELECT WHEN, EmitRunUseBody); KeyedIoBinder.cs uses ctx.Edition only as the diagnostic sink
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the two witnesses are a sequential-file VARYING/ADVANCING case and a DELETE INVALID KEY case; neither exercises an indexed WRITE's NOT INVALID KEY on 02, its 44/48 USE path, or INVALID KEY suppressing the USE procedure

probes.printed: OUTPUT dynamic: K050 OK 00; K010 (17 chars, ODO 3) OK 02 (DUPLICATES alternate); K010 dup prime IK 22; K020 dup no-DUPLICATES alternate IK 22; K030 30 chars OK 02; K040 length 11 -> USE 44, neither IK nor NOT IK; length 31 -> USE 44; WRITE without INVALID KEY on a dup prime -> USE 22, area K050A777D009 kept; I-O: K010 dup prime IK 22 (USE not run); K011 dup alternate IK 22; K005 OK 02; INPUT: USE 48; read back REC 12 K005..., REC 17 K010A010D00103XYZ, REC 30 K030A030D001160123456789ABCDEF, REC 12 K050...; USE COUNT 4
probes.expected: GR17b 22 in OUTPUT and I-O; GR17c 22 for a no-DUPLICATES alternate; IX-3 status 02 for an allowed duplicate; GR8 44; GR1 48; IX.1.3.5: INVALID KEY given -> USE not run, absent -> USE runs, a non-invalid-key exception -> USE and neither phrase; GR7 records read back with their own lengths

probes.printed: PCS IN RELATIONS: A > B / W M001 OK 00 (EXTEND on an empty file) / W A001 OK 00 / W B001 OK 00 / W B001 IK 21 AREA B001DUPKEY / W A999 IK 21 AREA A999LOWKEY / W C001 OK 00 / EXTEND: W C001 IK 21 (equal to highest) / W B999 IK 21 / W D001 OK 00 / W C500 IK 21 / FROM OK 00 / FROM IK 21 AREA D002AGAIN0 / read back: A001 B001 C001 D001 D002 only
probes.expected: GR14/GR17a: ascending native order (the program collating sequence REV, which puts B before A, does not apply to file keys: VI.4.4.4 GR7/GR8 list only relations, condition-names, CONTROL and SORT/MERGE); a key not greater than the previous one, or under EXTEND not greater than the highest existing key, is refused 21; GR18 record area unchanged; refused records absent

OK  §1985:IX.1.3.5 GR2  (1.3.5 The Invalid Key Condition)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: EmitPhrasePair runs INVALID KEY on the invalid-key class and NOT INVALID KEY on the successful class gated by the USE hook. The probes show NOT INVALID KEY on 00 and 02, INVALID KEY on 21/22 with the USE count unchanged, the USE procedure alone on 44 and 48, and on 22 when INVALID KEY is absent.

refuter.evidence: Probe r2use.cob (r2use-001, --std 85) tried what the reader did not: the applicable USE procedure chosen by open mode (USE ON OUTPUT, ON EXTEND, ON I-O, no file-name USE) when INVALID KEY is absent, and NOT INVALID KEY present on a failing WRITE. Output: 'USE-OUTPUT 21', 'USE-EXTEND 21 A500LOWEXT' with 'NOT-IK WRONG' never printed, 'NOT-IK 00' on success, 'USE-IO 22 K001DATA02'; control returns to the next statement after each USE. r1alt-001: NOT INVALID KEY runs on 02 and 00, INVALID KEY on 21/22. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR9  (4.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR9'; 'OK  §1985:IX.1.3.5  (1.3.5 The Invalid Key Condition)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GR3'.
